steps.description:
Read up the notes on TRY-EXCEPTION.

Click here to view the notes.

The instructor will then brief you on the topic.

Write a program that asks the user to input an integer. Using try-exception, if the number is an integer, display "valid" and end the program. Otherwise, display "invalid" and keep asking the user to input an integer.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input five 6.9 5

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the example below:

Input integer: five invalid Input integer: 6.9 invalid Input integer: 5 valid

Write a program that asks the user to input a negative integer. Using try-exception, if the number is a negative integer, display "valid" and end the program. Otherwise, display "invalid" and keep asking the user to input a negative integer.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input five 6.9 5 -100

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the example below:

Input negative integer: five invalid Input negative integer: 6.9 invalid Input negative integer: 5 invalid Input negative integer: -100 valid

Write a program that asks the user to input two float numbers in the format "x y". Using try-exception, display the result of x divided by y and end the program. If it is invalid, display "invalid" and asks the user to enter again.

Follow the test output display format.

Hint: - It is valid to enter a float without the decimal point - A number divided by zero will cause an error

Test Input 1.55 one 2.5 2.5 0.0 -1.05 2

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the example below:

Input 2 float numbers (x y): 1.55 invalid Input 2 float numbers (x y): one 2.5 invalid Input 2 float numbers (x y): 2.5 0.0 invalid Input 2 float numbers (x y): -1.05 2 -0.525

Write a program that asks the user to input an integer range in the format "x to y" (eg. 10 to 20 indicates the range from 10 to 20). Using try-exception, if the input is a valid integer range (from a smaller to a greater or equal number), display "valid" and end the program. Otherwise, display "invalid" and ask the user to enter again.

Follow the test output display format.

Hint: - It is valid to enter a float without the decimal point

Test Input 7 x to 7 7 to 10.5 99 to 1 -5 to -5

2.1 to 9 1 to 99

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Input an integer range (x to y): 7 invalid Input an integer range (x to y): x to 7 invalid Input an integer range (x to y): 7 to 10.5 invalid Input an integer range (x to y): 99 to 1 invalid Input an integer range (x to y): -5 to -5 valid

Input an integer range (x to y): 2.1 to 9 invalid Input an integer range (x to y): 1 to 99 valid

Write a program that does the following: 1. asks user to input the length of a rectangle. The length must be a positive float number. If it is not, display "invalid length" and asks user to re-enter the length. 2. asks user to input the breadth of a rectangle. The breadth must be a positive float number. If it is not, display "invalid breadth" and asks user to re-enter the breadth. 3. display the area of the rectangle round up to 1 decimal place and end the program.

Follow the test output display format.

Hint: - It is valid to enter a float without the decimal point

Test Input ten -5 10.999 two 0 2

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the example below:

Input length of rectangle: ten invalid length Input length of rectangle: -5 invalid length Input length of rectangle: 10.999 Input breadth of rectangle: two invalid breadth Input breadth of rectangle: -6.3 invalid breadth Input breadth of rectangle: 2 Area of rectangle is 22.0
